intro: A distributional value model stores probability mass on fixed return atoms. A Bellman update shifts those atoms, so mass must be projected back without losing it.
task: Transform each return atom and distribute its mass between neighboring support points. Inspect exact-grid hits and clipping at the support endpoints.
requirements: probabilities and atoms are equal-length vectors with 2..256 entries. Probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one within absolute tolerance 1e-8. atoms are strictly increasing, equally spaced within atol=1e-10 and rtol=1e-10, and their spacing is at least 1e-8.

reward is a scalar, discount is in [0,1], and terminal is integer 0 or 1. For each atom z compute clipped=clip(reward+discount*(1-terminal)*z,atoms[0],atoms[-1]). Split its probability linearly between neighboring grid points.
Return a probability NumPy vector on the original atoms. If the transformed point lands exactly on a grid location, put all its mass there; do not multiply it by two zero interpolation weights.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Locate the actual neighbors
hints.body: Search the sorted supplied atoms for the bounding pair, then interpolate by their actual distance. This also handles spacing differences within the stated tolerance.

hints.title: Handle exact hits separately
hints.body: When the lower and upper bin coincide, the entire source mass goes to that bin.

explanation: Projection preserves total probability and the clipped transformed expectation. Support clipping can change the unbounded Bellman expectation, so the support is a modeling choice.

Terminal updates collapse the future distribution to the reward, but a reward between two support points still occupies two bins. This is the categorical projection used by distributional methods, with an arbitrary support size.
